claim: The number of ionizable-lipid tail lengths in the library
locus_A: Results, 'Generation of LNP Library': 'multitail structures with varying tail lengths (C10, C12, and C13) and different stereoisomers, as well as cKK-E12'
locus_B: Methods, 'LNP Formulation': 'The ionizable lipids used in this study were stereopure lipomers (C12S, C12R, C13S, and C13R ...), MC3 ... and cKK-E12' -- no C10. Figure 1A's 'R Chains' key likewise lists only C12S/C13S/C12R/C13R with R = C12H25 / C13H27.
measurement: two independent loci (Methods list, Figure 1A key) name four lipomers and no C10; one locus (Results prose) names three tail lengths including C10
what_we_emitted: nothing -- no stereopure lipomer is emitted, so the discrepancy touches no value
why: The Results sentence is the only place C10 appears. We do not resolve it; we record that the library's distinct-structure count is therefore not determinable from the paper.

claim: The QC diameter cut-off for admitting an LNP to the in vivo screen
locus_A: <200 nm, stated three times: Figure 1C caption ('diameter less than 200 nm'), Results ('hydrodynamic diameter <200 nm'), and Methods ML section ('non-QC-passed LNPs (>200 nm) were not included')
locus_B: Methods, 'LNP Characterization': inclusion required '(i) diameter >20 nm, (ii) diameter <150 nm, (iii) correlation function with one inflection point, and (iv) PDI < 0.4'
measurement: RETIRED BY THE DATA. Figure 1D plots the diameters of all administered LNPs on a 0-200 nm axis and a substantial fraction of the points lie between 150 and ~195 nm. A <150 nm criterion is therefore not the one that was applied.
what_we_emitted: nothing -- no emitted row depends on the QC threshold; the six leads' own diameters are in Figure 2A, which we do not use
why: Recorded because a reader reconstructing the 150-of-99 selection from the Methods would get a different library.

claim: The percentage of aVHH+ LECs for a given LNP and node
locus_A: SI Table S2 / S3 / S4: average LEC count and average aVHH+ cell count, whose ratio is a RATIO OF MEANS
locus_B: Figures 2B-D and 4A and the running text: one point per independent experiment and the mean of those per-animal percentages, a MEAN OF RATIOS
measurement: 17 printed percentages compared against the derived ratio of means. Spearman 0.820641; 10 of 17 within 3 percentage points; worst is Fig 2 BLN LNP1, derived 17.58% against printed 44%, ratio 0.40. The two are different statistics and are not expected to be equal.
what_we_emitted: the RATIO OF MEANS, because it is the only per-formulation number derivable from published material, with this stated in curation_note on all 28 rows
why: Neither source is rescaled onto the other and no average of the two is taken.

claim: How much better than the MC3 benchmark the lead LNP is at the draining popliteal node
locus_A: running text: 'saline 2%, free aVHH 2%, MC3 5%, LNP7 31%' -- a 6.2x advantage
locus_B: SI Tables S3/S4 ratio of means: MC3 14.005%, LNP7 33.518% -- a 2.393x advantage
measurement: ratio of the two advantage factors = 2.59. The same class as C-3, but singled out because it is the benchmark: the three other printed values at that site reproduce within 2.5 points (saline 3.00 vs 2, free 1.90 vs 2, LNP7 33.52 vs 31) and only MC3 moves. At the popliteal lymphatic VESSEL the two agree (MC3 9.52 vs printed 10).
what_we_emitted: the derived 14.005%, flagged like every other row
why: A single MC3 animal with a high aVHH+ monocyte and LEC count would move the ratio of means far more than the mean of ratios; the same row shows 25,134 monocytes against 599 in saline. We do not have per-animal data to confirm it.

claim: LNP7's % aVHH+ LECs in the axillary and brachial nodes
locus_A: SI Table S2 (Figure 2 cohort): ALN 35.44%, BLN 33.71%
locus_B: SI Tables S3/S4 (Figure 4 cohort): ALN 2.46%, BLN 3.88%
measurement: RETIRED. Ratios 14.4x and 8.7x, which looked like a flat contradiction. The paper states that the Figure 4 study 'injected only one hindlimb, which allowed us to use the lymph nodes that drain the remaining limbs as controls for off-target delivery', while the Figure 2 study injected both paws. So ALN and BLN drain an injected paw in one cohort and not in the other. The one site that drains the injection in BOTH, the popliteal node, agrees: 37.34% vs 33.52%, ratio 1.114.
what_we_emitted: both, with Model_target carrying '_nondraining' on the three study-B control sites so the two cannot collapse under one key
why: The 1.114 popliteal ratio is also the evidence that ONE z-block over both cohorts is correct rather than two (error class 22 / F-016).

claim: (RETRACTED SUSPICION, and it was ours, not the paper's) that the derived percentages disagreed with the printed ones by up to 12.9x
locus_A: first run of stage08_qc.py's derived_ratio_of_means_vs_printed_mean_of_ratios: Fig 2 ALN LNP1 derived 188.21% against printed 45%
locus_B: stage05_values.py, which computed the same cell as 53.13%
measurement: RETIRED BY ARITHMETIC. The check had unpacked SI Table S2's (LEC count, aVHH+ count) pair in the wrong order and divided LEC by aVHH+. Both are plain integers and the ratio stays finite, so nothing raised; the defect was visible only because the comparison against the paper's own printed percentages was there to expose it, which it did at 12.9x, and because percentages above 100 are impossible. Fixed; the column order is now stated at the point of unpacking.
what_we_emitted: unaffected -- stage05_values.py, which produces every emitted value, always had the order right
why: Kept because it is the measurement that retired the suspicion, and because it is a concrete instance of why a check needs an external comparison rather than internal consistency.
